description: An SRE (Site Reliability Engineer) faces a production outage. Conflict: The logs suggest a database timeout, but the DB dashboard shows low load. The conflict lies in a hidden network latency issue in the cloud provider's regional zone.

user_profile.communication_style: Concise, data-heavy, focused on Root Cause Analysis

fact_sheet.fact: Incident QLA-INC-20240523-001 was declared on May 23, 2024, at 14:02 UTC.
The incident was classified as Severity-1 (SEV-1), indicating a critical production outage affecting external customers.
The 'QuantumLeap Analytics' user dashboard and data ingestion API (api.quantumleap.io) are returning HTTP 503 Service Unavailable errors.
The first alert was triggered by the Prometheus monitoring system with the message: 'HighErrorRate: Job core-processor-svc has a 5xx error rate > 80%'.
The designated Incident Commander is Maya Singh, Director of Engineering.
The primary on-call Site Reliability Engineer responding to the incident is Alex Chen.
The primary communication channel for the incident is the Slack channel #inc-20240523-sev1-api-outage.
The incident war room is hosted on a persistent video conference link: meet.quantumleap.io/war-room-alpha.
The company experiencing the outage is QuantumLeap Analytics, a B2B data insights provider.
All affected infrastructure is hosted on AetherCloud Services (ACS) in the us-east-4 region.
The primary microservice experiencing failures is the 'core-processor-svc', running on Docker version 25.0.3.
The service connects to a ChronoDB managed database cluster, version 12.5.
The 'core-processor-svc' instances are deployed exclusively in the us-east-4a availability zone.
Application logs for 'core-processor-svc' show repeated entries of 'Error: Connection timeout expired while connecting to database endpoint chrono-prod-1.c4xyz123.us-east-4.rds.aethercloud.com:5432'.
Centralized logging is managed by LogStashPro, accessible at logs.quantumleap.io.
At the peak of the incident, 92% of API requests to 'core-processor-svc' were failing.
The first database timeout error was logged at 13:58:15 UTC, four minutes before the SEV-1 was declared.
The ChronoDB dashboard shows CPU utilization on the primary instance is stable at 18%.
The number of active database connections is 35, well below the configured maximum of 500.
Database Read/Write IOPS are averaging 1,200, which is 30% of the provisioned capacity.
A 'ping' from a 'core-processor-svc' container to the database endpoint shows an average RTT of 250ms with 15% packet loss.
An 'mtr' trace from a service instance to the DB endpoint revealed a high latency hop (avg 245ms) within the 10.40.1.0/24 subnet, internal to the us-east-4a zone.
The network monitoring tool 'NetFlow-Analyzer' confirmed a 15-20% packet loss rate for traffic between subnets in us-east-4a.
The AetherCloud Services status page was updated at 14:35 UTC to acknowledge 'Intermittent Packet Loss within a single Availability Zone in the US-EAST-4 Region.'
The root cause was identified as a degraded network fabric switch within the ACS us-east-4a availability zone.
The immediate resolution was to initiate a blue-green deployment, failing over all 'core-processor-svc' traffic to new instances in the us-east-4b availability zone.
The failover process was completed at 14:51 UTC, and service health was confirmed by 14:55 UTC.
A blameless post-mortem for incident QLA-INC-20240523-001 is scheduled for May 24, 2024, at 15:00 UTC.
An action item was created for the SRE team lead, David Rodriguez, to implement a multi-AZ deployment strategy for 'core-processor-svc' by Q3 2024.
